bib.title: 7. Learning in Agentic Systems | Building Applications with AI Agents
bib.venue: book chapter (Building Applications with AI Agents, chapter 7)

question: How can agentic systems improve through interaction, via nonparametric methods (exemplars, Reflexion, ExpeL-style insights) or parametric fine-tuning (SFT, DPO, RLVR), and when is each worth the cost?

limits: No experiments of its own; code examples are illustrative and no outputs or metrics are shown.
Reflexion, ExpeL, SFT, DPO and RLVR are named with no citations or arXiv ids in the chapter text.
RLVR is described as combining preference learning with value prediction; the full RLVR code is deferred to an unnamed accompanying repository.
Model rankings (HELM, Phi-3, GPT-5, Llama 3, Qwen2.5) are dated by the authors' own admission: the best small model may be eclipsed within months.
The DPO listing is partial in the PDF (uses undefined ds, reference_free=True with ref_model=None, an unused TrainingArguments), so it is not runnable as printed.
practices: Treat learning as optional: it needs extra design, evaluation and monitoring (chapter intro).
Start with nonparametric methods (exemplars, Reflexion, insights) before fine-tuning because they are simpler and faster (Parametric Learning).
Move from fixed few-shot examples to dynamic retrieval of the most relevant successful examples as examples accumulate (Exemplar Learning).
For Reflexion, feed only the last 3 reflections into the reflection prompt to bound context (code, update_memory).
Maintain an insight list with ADD, EDIT, REMOVE and AGREE operations, promoting and demoting rules over time (Experiential Learning).

Fine-tune only when domain specialisation, consistent format, precise tool calls, enough data and budget, and manageable retraining frequency hold; fine-tuning needs hundreds to thousands of curated examples.
Hold off on fine-tuning during prototyping, low volume, resource limits, or when upstream model upgrades may erase the gain; when in doubt, do not fine-tune.
Prefer an open-source, already instruction-tuned model over pretraining; pretraining is for major labs only.
For tool use, start with built-in function calling and runtime schema validation; use SFT on tool-call data only if those fall short.
Define each tool in JSON Schema or Zod, include schemas in fine-tuning data, and validate every proposed call at runtime (Pydantic, Ajv, Zod).
Use special tokens such as <think> and <tool_call> to separate dialogue, reasoning and action in SFT data.
Use LoRA with 4-bit quantised base and SFTTrainer for cheap SFT (listing).
Use DPO when the goal is output quality (tone, style, summarisation) rather than replicating gold outputs.
Use RLVR when any reliable grader or scoring function can be built.
Track small-model choices on third-party leaderboards (HELM, Papers With Code, HF Evaluation on the Hub, BigBench); under 8B for on-device, 8B-70B for general reasoning.

terms.definition: improving the performance of the agentic system through interaction with the environment
techniques to change and improve performance automatically without changing the parameters of the models involved
techniques in which we specifically train or fine-tune the parameters of the foundation model
agent is given a measure of quality and successful examples are used as few-shot examples for in-context learning
after each unsuccessful attempt the agent writes a brief reflection on what went wrong, kept in a memory buffer and reread before the next attempt
aggregating insights across stored experiences into a list of rules that are added, edited, upvoted, downvoted or removed; adds cross-task learning to Reflexion
curated (prompt, response) pairs that teach the model how it should behave
trains a model to prefer better outputs over worse ones by learning from ranked pairs
expert-graded outputs and policy-gradient updates to reinforce complex reasoning chains
policy optimization against an explicit, measurable reward function from any grader you can build
